Accents varied per pick since all five share the single 'movies' category.

picks.title: LTX releases LTX-2.5, an open-weights video world model studios can run on their own hardware
picks.excerpt: LTX released LTX-2.5, an open-weights video world model studios can run on their own hardware, keeping IP and prompts in-house. It handles ACES HDR end to end and renders multishot sequences as a single output; available now via Hugging Face, the LTX API and ComfyUI.
picks.rationale: Open weights plus end-to-end ACES HDR and single-pass multishot output is the first generative video model that drops straight into an on-prem color-managed pipeline.

picks.title: Reallusion launches AccuFACE 2, production-grade markerless facial mocap from a webcam or iPhone
picks.excerpt: Reallusion launched AccuFACE 2, an AI-driven markerless facial mocap system aimed at production-grade performance capture for CC5 HD characters from ordinary webcam or iPhone capture. It targets small teams doing character animation without a mocap stage.
picks.rationale: Performance capture without a stage: a small animation team can shoot facial mocap tomorrow with hardware already on the desk.

picks.title: SubtitleNext wires AssemblyAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Whisper into subtitling, plus IMSCR and batch runs
picks.excerpt: Profuz Digital's SubtitleNext adds expanded AI transcription integrations with AssemblyAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Whisper, plus IMSCR support and batch processing for subtitle and audio-description work. It points at AI moving into routine localization pipelines rather than hero shots.
picks.rationale: AI lands where the hours actually go — four ASR engines plus batch processing rewrites the economics of subtitle and audio-description passes.

picks.title: Roku's Fairground AI is a 24/7 free channel programmed entirely with AI-generated shorts
picks.excerpt: Roku launched Fairground AI, a 24/7 free channel programmed entirely with AI-generated narrative shorts and commercials. It's the first mainstream US distribution slot built purely for synthetic video, and a live read on whether audiences will sit with it.
picks.rationale: The first mainstream US distribution slot reserved for synthetic video — a real audience test, and a place AI-native shorts can actually land.

picks.title: Runway's Ruby outputs 16-bit HDR ProRes and EXR from any video model, not just its own
picks.excerpt: Runway introduced Ruby, a model that generates 16-bit HDR ProRes and EXR sequences directly, or converts existing clips and generations into them. It is model-agnostic — compatible with Gen-4.5, Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3 and other video models — so generative shots can enter a color-managed grade/comp pipeline instead of stopping at 8-bit delivery files.
picks.rationale: Kills the 8-bit dead end that keeps AI shots out of the grade — any model's output can now arrive as 16-bit ProRes or EXR ready for comp.
